title: Closed subschemes are limits of their stage scheme-theoretic images
statement: Let $J$ be a small nonempty cofiltered category and $D:J\to\mathsf{Scheme}$ a diagram of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose every $D_j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated (the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact), and every transition morphism is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\pi_Y$ be a limit cone with vertex $Y$ and let $i:X\to Y$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then there exist a diagram $Z:J\to\mathsf{Scheme}$, a natural transformation $k:Z\to D$ with closed immersion components, and a cone $\pi_X$ with vertex $X$, such that $X$ is its limit, every transition of $Z$ is affine, and $\pi_{X,j}\mathbin{;}k_j=i\mathbin{;}\pi_{Y,j}$ for every $j\in J$ (composition written in diagram order).

proof.text: Let I_j = ker(i followed by πY_j), and Z_j = I_j.subscheme. Naturality and map_ker identify I_l with I_j.map(D(a)) for each arrow a:j→l. Use subschemeMap to define the transition maps, subschemeι for k, and toImage for πX. Cancellation by the monomorphic subscheme inclusions proves functor laws and naturality, and toImage_imageι gives the factorization equations.

Reconstruct ker(i) as the supremum K of I_j.comap(πY_j). The inequality K≤ker(i) is the map/comap Galois connection and map_ker. For the reverse inequality, fix a stage j0 and the affine open cover of D_j0. Projections are affine, so its pullback covers Y by affine opens W. Over an affine open U of D_j0, use the cofinal over-category diagram opensDiagram and its limit opensCone. All of its stages are affine; the section-surjectivity clause of the coordinate-ring colimit theorem, in Mathlib exists_appTop_π_eq_of_isAffine_of_isLimit, lifts any section s of ker(i) on W to a section t on an affine inverse image V in some D_j. Naturality identifies πY_j inverse-image V with W. Since i.app(W)(s)=0, compatibility of appLE with composition and the invertible restriction for this equality of opens show (i followed by πY_j).app(V)(t)=0. Quasi-compactness gives ker_apply, so t belongs to I_j. The Galois connection puts I_j inside K.map(πY_j); ideal_map_of_isAffineHom and restriction of ideals put s inside K(W). IdealSheafData.le_of_iSup_eq_top glues these inclusions. Hence ker(i)=K.

For a test cone s on Z, compose with k and use hY.lift to obtain m:s.pt→Y. Each I_j is contained in ker(s.π_j followed by k_j) by le_ker_comp and ker_subschemeι. The Galois connection, the cone equations hY.fac, and ker(i)=K therefore give ker(i)≤ker(m). IsClosedImmersion.lift factors m through i. Monicity of k_j proves its cone equations; monicity of i and hY.hom_ext prove uniqueness. This constructs IsLimit (Cone.mk X πX) directly, without constructing a limit of quotient rings.

For a transition a:j→l, its composite with k_l is k_j followed by D(a), which is affine as a composite of affine morphisms. The closed immersion k_l is separated, so Mathlib IsAffineHom.of_comp makes the transition affine. This is the standard separated-target cancellation argument: factor through the graph (a base change of the closed diagonal) followed by the affine base-change projection. The k_j are closed immersions by the subschemeι instance. Together with the constructed limit and factorization equations this proves the stated existential.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_closed_image_limit_system
    {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (D : J ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {j k : J} (a : j ⟶ k), IsAffineHom (D.map a)]
    [∀ j : J, CompactSpace (D.obj j)]
    [∀ j : J, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj j)]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (πY : (Functor.const J).obj Y ⟶ D) (hY : IsLimit (Cone.mk Y πY)) :
    ∃ (Z : J ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (k : Z ⟶ D)
      (πX : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ Z),
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X πX)) ∧
      (∀ {j k : J} (a : j ⟶ k), IsAffineHom (Z.map a)) ∧
      (∀ j : J, IsClosedImmersion (k.app j)) ∧
      (∀ j : J, πX.app j ≫ k.app j = i ≫ πY.app j)
